title: Procedure
description: An execution graph of typed steps run by an AIP server with the client in the loop. Step kinds are `start` (the procedure's inputs, what the client supplies), `decision` (SystemOne questions answered by a structured decision model), `execution` (a script under scripts/), `client_task` (templated work the client performs itself), `router` (server-side branching on a value the client chose) and `end` (the procedure's result). Edges are `inputs_to` by step name. Every runnable step declares the keys it reads as `inputs`; execution and client_task steps declare the keys they add as `outputs`, and a decision's outputs are its question names plus a `<question>_confidence` for each question its `confidence` list names. Keys accumulate and a later step may overwrite one; every declaration of a key agrees on its type.

type.description: Pick one label from a set.
type.title: Type

instructions.description: What to pick between and how to judge. The answer is the most likely label plus the full probability distribution; it collapses to the label under the question name.
instructions.title: Instructions

criteria.description: Label to description. Null when the label is self-explanatory. Router branches keyed on this question use these labels.
criteria.title: Criteria

name.description: Short kebab-case identifier, unique within the procedure. Edges (`inputs_to`, router `branches`) reference steps by this name.
name.title: Name

kind.description: The client performs the work itself: generation, synthesis, reasoning.
kind.title: Kind

description.description: What the client is asked to do. One line; the template carries the detail.
description.title: Description

inputs.description: The keys this step reads from the state; every listed name is required. Each must be produced by a step on every path to this one, or declared on the start step, whose inputs are what the client supplies.
inputs.title: Inputs

template.description: The task template, rendered with `{key}` placeholders from the input, `{assets[name]}` for injected assets, and `{meta.name}` for the skill name. The client performs the task and answers with structured JSON matching the step's `outputs`.
template.title: Template

outputs.description: The keys the client's answer adds to the state. Required: they are what the client is asked to answer with.
outputs.title: Outputs

assets.description: Extra assets available to the template as `{assets[name]}`, where name is the file stem.

items.description: Path under `assets/`, relative to the skill folder. Assets are eager: their content is injected on every invoke.

assets.title: Assets

references.description: Documents the client may load on demand while doing the task.
references.title: References

framing.description: Prepend the AIP system framing (which workflow this is, how to read the state) to the rendered task.
framing.title: Framing

inputs_to.description: The step that receives this step's output.
inputs_to.title: Inputs To

key.description: A `float` key in the state, declared on a path to the router: typically a decision's `<question>_confidence`.
key.title: Key

below.description: The bound. The check fires when the key's value is below it, or when the key is absent or null: unknown confidence is low confidence, and nobody invents a number.
below.title: Below

to.description: The step the run goes to when the check fires.
to.title: To

DataType.description:
AIP type vocabulary. Machine-enforced at runtime: the server compiles each step's
`inputs` and `outputs` to JSON Schemas and validates the state and the step's result against them.
DataType.title: DataType

name.description: Short kebab-case identifier, unique within the procedure. Edges (`inputs_to`, router `branches`) reference steps by this name.
name.title: Name

kind.description: A structured decision model answers typed questions about the input.
kind.title: Kind

description.description: What this decision settles. One line.
description.title: Description

inputs.description: The keys this step reads from the state; every listed name is required. Each must be produced by a step on every path to this one, or declared on the start step, whose inputs are what the client supplies.
inputs.title: Inputs

questions.description: Questions keyed by name. Answers come back under the same names and, once collapsed, become keys in the state: a decision's outputs are its question names.

^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$.description: One SystemOne question. `instructions` carry the evaluation criteria; the step's input is the content being evaluated. Passed through to the decision model as-is.

questions.title: Questions

confidence.description: Question names whose confidence the step also emits. For each, `<question>_confidence` is added to the state beside the answer as a `float` in `[0, 1]`: the probability the decision model put on the answer it gave, which is its confidence for a `choice` or `score` and `|2p - 1|` for a `noul`. An answer given by hand writes no confidence key.
confidence.title: Confidence

fallback.description: Whether the client may answer the questions by hand when no decision model is configured. Off by default: a run with no model stops at this step. On, a manual answer carries no confidence, so a router's confidence check on it fires.
fallback.title: Fallback

history.description: Send the run's history (every earlier step's input and result) to the decision model alongside the declared inputs. Off by default: history grows with the run and is billed on every decision.
history.title: History

inputs_to.description: The step that receives this step's output.
inputs_to.title: Inputs To

name.description: Short kebab-case identifier, unique within the procedure. Edges (`inputs_to`, router `branches`) reference steps by this name.
name.title: Name

description.description: What the final state represents. One line.
description.title: Description

inputs.description: The procedure's result: the keys handed back to the client when the run is done.
inputs.title: Inputs

name.description: Short kebab-case identifier, unique within the procedure. Edges (`inputs_to`, router `branches`) reference steps by this name.
name.title: Name

kind.description: A script runs. Analogous to a tool call.
kind.title: Kind

description.description: What the script does. One line; the script is the source of truth.
description.title: Description

inputs.description: The keys this step reads from the state; every listed name is required. Each must be produced by a step on every path to this one, or declared on the start step, whose inputs are what the client supplies.
inputs.title: Inputs

script.description: Path under `scripts/`, relative to the skill folder. Receives one JSON object on stdin ({state, assets, expects}, where `state` holds only the step's declared `inputs`) and writes one JSON object to stdout holding exactly the step's `outputs`.
script.title: Script

outputs.description: The keys this step adds to the state. A key may have more than one producer, and a later step may overwrite one; every declaration of a key agrees on its type.
outputs.title: Outputs

command.description: How the script is launched, as an argument list run from the script's folder: `["bash", "run.sh"]`. Omitted, it is `python` on the script. The first item must be the `requires` interpreter or one of its `tools`.
command.title: Command

assets.description: Constant inputs the script always receives, such as a config file. Re-read from disk on every invoke.

items.description: Path under `assets/`, relative to the skill folder. Assets are eager: their content is injected on every invoke.

assets.title: Assets

timeout.description: Seconds before the script is killed. Defaults to the server's setting when omitted.
timeout.title: Timeout

inputs_to.description: The step that receives this step's output.
inputs_to.title: Inputs To

name.description: Key in the state. In `inputs`, a key the step reads; in `outputs`, a key the step adds. Decision answers land under their question name, so a downstream step that consumes an answer declares an input of the same name.
name.title: Name

type.description: Type from the AIP vocabulary. Enforced on the state before the step runs (inputs) and on the step's result (outputs).

description.description: One-line summary of what this value is. Optional but recommended: it makes the graph readable without opening the backing script or template.
description.title: Description

name.description: The program that runs the scripts, as found on PATH: `python`, `bash`, `node`. Execution steps without a `command` are launched with `python`.
name.title: Name

version.description: Minimum version, dotted numbers (`3.10`). For `python` it is checked against the interpreter that runs the scripts; for anything else against the first version number `<name> --version` prints.
version.title: Version

true.description: What counts as a yes answer.
true.title: True

false.description: What counts as a no answer.
false.title: False

instructions.description: A yes/no question or statement about the input. The answer is a probability of yes/true; it collapses to a boolean under the question name.
instructions.title: Instructions

criteria.description: Optional sharpening of what counts as yes and no.

path.description: Path under `references/`, relative to the skill folder. References are lazy: the client receives the path and description and fetches the body only if it decides it needs it.
path.title: Path

description.description: What the reference contains and when to pull it. This is all the client sees before deciding to load it.
description.title: Description

Requires.description:
What the machine that runs the scripts must have. The client checks it before the first
execution step and stops with one message naming every missing item.

interpreter.description: The interpreter the scripts need, with its minimum version.

packages.description: Python distributions the scripts import, as installed by pip (`numpy`, `scikit-learn>=1.3`), optionally with a minimum version. Checked in the interpreter that runs `python` scripts.
packages.title: Packages

tools.description: Other executables the scripts call or are launched with, each checked on PATH (`git`, `ffmpeg`, `bash`).
tools.title: Tools

Requires.title: Requires

name.description: Short kebab-case identifier, unique within the procedure. Edges (`inputs_to`, router `branches`) reference steps by this name.
name.title: Name

kind.description: Server-side branch on a value the client chose. Calls no model, has no endpoint.
kind.title: Kind

description.description: What the branch decides. One line.
description.title: Description

branch_on.description: Key in the state whose value selects the branch: a `boolean`, `string` or `integer`, typically a decision question name or an output of an execution or client task. The router adds nothing to the state; its choice is recorded in the run history only.
branch_on.title: Branch On

confidence.description: Optional confidence check, applied before `branches`: when `key` is below `below`, absent or null, the run goes to `to` and the value match is skipped. One check per router; a router that needs more is two routers.

additionalProperties.description: Short kebab-case identifier, unique within the procedure. Edges (`inputs_to`, router `branches`) reference steps by this name.

branches.description: Value to step name. The server resolves this after the client posts; the client never traverses. A value with no branch is a validation error.
branches.title: Branches

type.description: Rate the input on an ordered rubric.
type.title: Type

instructions.description: What is being rated. The answer is a probability-weighted position on the rubric; it collapses to the most likely integer level under the question name.
instructions.title: Instructions

criteria.description: Ordered rubric, lowest level first. Level numbers are the list positions starting at 0.
criteria.title: Criteria

name.description: Short kebab-case identifier, unique within the procedure. Edges (`inputs_to`, router `branches`) reference steps by this name.
name.title: Name

kind.description: Where a run begins. Holds the procedure's inputs and hands them to the first runnable step. Not runnable, adds nothing of its own.
kind.title: Kind

description.description: What the client supplies to start a run. One line.
description.title: Description

inputs.description: The procedure's inputs: the keys the client supplies to start a run. They are the initial state.
inputs.title: Inputs

purpose.description: What the procedure encapsulates as a coherent unit of work: the scope it covers and what it adds beyond general agent knowledge. One short paragraph.
purpose.title: Purpose

trigger_when.description: Conditions under which the agent should consider this skill. Mixed granularity expected: immediate invocation triggers alongside broader applicability contexts belong in the same list.
trigger_when.title: Trigger When

do_not_use_when.description: Conditions under which the agent should NOT use this skill: explicit non-purposes that pair with trigger_when to sharpen activation.
do_not_use_when.title: Do Not Use When

requires.description: The environment the scripts need: interpreter and minimum version, Python packages, other tools. Required when the procedure has execution steps.

steps.description: The nodes of the execution graph. Exactly one step has kind `start` (by convention the first) and exactly one has kind `end`. Every runnable step names the node that receives its output via `inputs_to`; routers name theirs via `branches` and their confidence check's `to`. The validator checks that names are unique, every reference resolves, nothing points at the start, every step is reachable from the start, every step can reach the end, every consumed key is produced on every path to its consumer or declared on the start step, every declaration of a key agrees on its type, a router branches on a `boolean`, `string` or `integer` and checks a `float`, a procedure with execution steps declares `requires` and launches each script with its interpreter or one of its tools, and every referenced asset, reference, and script exists on disk.
steps.title: Steps

anti_patterns.description: Common mistakes the procedure steers the agent away from. Concrete corrections to errors the agent would otherwise make.
anti_patterns.title: Anti Patterns
